content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text gives an UNDERDETERMINED verdict on Matthew 1:20 based on the verse's own source statement and a footed analogy, so it decides whether a two-sense verse may remain open.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb; answered in [CR3] LINK 2.","rule_words":"A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. I weighed whether the verse's own source statement plus the footed covenant-origin analogy are two senses, which would bar UNDERDETERMINED, or whether the judge merely weighs a verse statement against an analogy, which would not.","why":"The judge labels Matthew 1:20 UNDERDETERMINED while acknowledging both the footed covenant-origin analogy and the verse's own source statement, treating the two-sense verse as open instead of letting both senses stand."}
